archetype: Azorius flash control whose commander is a converter, not a threat: the table is gifted cards, Heliod, the Warped Eclipse turns those draws into a per-spell discount that lives on the opponents' turns, and the game is won by the second cast of Approach of the Second Sun. deck-audit reads `control` from strategic_frame.json and the slot budget agrees (interaction 14 of 12-15, protection 5 of 5-7, ramp 12 of 10-12, card-advantage 16 of >=10); the conversion is a one-finisher combo deck's, and every count below is read against that.
verdict: The deck wins by casting Approach of the Second Sun twice and by almost nothing else: over the 99 decided games of run b0f44e4a, 12 of 12 games that reached a second cast won against 8 of 87 that did not (1 of 10 on a single cast, 7 of 77 on none) — a ratio close to DEFINITIONAL, since Approach wins on resolution and across 39 casts the logs show no counterspell ever aimed at one. WHAT THE FORGE RECORD DOES NOT ESTABLISH IS WHY THE DECK GETS THERE, and both of this document's earlier attempts to say are withdrawn. The commander does not predict winning (resolving 13/68 = 0.191 against 7/52 = 0.135, Newcombe ci95 [-0.1849, +0.0838]; flipping 6/35 against 14/85, ci95 [-0.1748, +0.1230]), and neither does mana once the confound is controlled properly: the land gap between Approach-cast and no-Approach games disappears on the seat's OWN turns (0.8178 against 0.7849, ci95 [-0.0960, +0.0301]) and among the 46 games heliod was not eliminated in (lands ci95 [-2.5120, +0.6152]), because elimination differs 0.33 against 0.70 between those arms. Lands do not separate the 12 two-cast games from the 15 one-cast games at all. SO THE PRESCRIPTION RESTS ON THE DETERMINISTIC SHORTFALL AND NOT ON A CROSS-TAB: 33 lands against the control band of 37-39, 25 white and 26 blue sources against Karsten's 36, benchmark.json's missed-land-drop rate of 0.2568 worst at turn six, and a finisher costing seven mana twice. Mana-base binds on the audit's own figures; win-condition access is second and its final step is unexplained; protection is adequate and is bought below against a measured exit table.

Gift plus drain, both drawn: 0.32, gated by the two-card drain half. Not prescribed against — the drain is not how this deck wins.
The asymmetry layer with Heliod down: 0.787, 0.583 by turn six. The right kind of card and enough of them.
Counters held: 0.839, 0.705 by turn six, mean turn 3.022. A counter answers a wrath on the way in and a Swords in a stack war only if it wins the war; log 001 is the game where it did not.

An X-spell drawn: 0.792. Whether X is chosen before or after Heliod's reduction applies is an open stack question, and so is the line that matters more — an X-draw aimed at opponents on their end step as the discount for Approach itself.

Win-condition access: 0.495 assembled, 0.358 by turn six, 0.199 in an opener — and the component that decides the game. 27 of 120 games cast Approach once, 12 twice, and all 12 won. What separates 12 from 15 is NOT measurable here: lands (9.58 vs 9.67), global turn (41.17 vs 43.20) and tutor casts (0.75 vs 0.80) all span zero on n=12 against n=15.

Heliod protected or a flash grant without him: 0.683, 0.531 by turn six. Leyline protects nothing and duplicates only the flash half of the converter; Greaves' shroud is one of the deck's own open rules questions; Forge never cast Guardian of Faith or Teferi's Protection, so the run cannot speak to this group.
A body that blocks a flier: 0.68, and 43 of 61 damage eliminations came from giada-angels. Kefnet blocks only at seven cards in hand; the other four block unconditionally.

A taxer down: 0.496, 0.357 by turn six, 0.199 in an opener. Thin, and the least reliable defensive group; not prescribed against here because the Forge run could not detect the fort moving anything (eliminations 74 of 120 in both v1.0.0 and v1.2.1 runs).

open_questions.question: What separates the 12 games that cast Approach of the Second Sun twice from the 15 that cast it once? Lands (9.58 vs 9.67, ci95 [-2.054, +2.221]), lands per own turn (ci95 [-0.0744, +0.1539]), global turn (41.17 vs 43.20) and tutor casts (0.75 vs 0.80) all span zero at n=12 against n=15, so the step that actually wins the game is unexplained and the verdict says so rather than asserting a chain through it.
open_questions.why_it_matters: 12 of 12 decided games reaching a second cast won and 8 of 87 otherwise. Every add in this document that is not a land is sized off the assumption that ACCESS is the missing step; if the real gate is mana in one window, or the seven-card gap between the first cast and the shuffle, the tutors buy less than claimed.

open_questions.question: With Heliod, the Warped Eclipse on the battlefield, cast Prosperity or Skyscribing for X on an opponent's end step and then Approach of the Second Sun in the same window: what does Approach cost under 'Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn', and does the 'cast from your hand' win condition survive a flash cast?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the pilot's 'two or three, not seven' from log 002 and the reason the two symmetric X-draws are kept while Mathemagics and Braingeyser are cut. It is also the one line that would make the flip worth protecting, which the win-rate split currently does not.

open_questions.question: While Lightning Greaves is attached to Heliod, can Karametra's Blessing or Guardian of Faith's enters trigger target him, and can the Greaves be moved off at instant speed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Greaves-for-Boots swap is priced on the answer being 'no'. If shroud does not bind the pilot's own spells the way this document reads it, Greaves keeps its slot on equip {0}.

open_questions.question: Time Wipe with Heliod, the Warped Eclipse transformed on the battlefield: which face returns to hand, is the transformation lost, and can the returned card be recast the same turn under Leyline of Anticipation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Time Wipe's rebuy mode is the whole of its case over Day of Judgment, and its extra blue pip taxes the axis this diagnosis calls binding.

open_questions.question: Re-declare goldfish_targets.json: add Mind Stone to the flip group's any_of (it pays the {3} of {3}{U/P} identically and is omitted), add Solve the Equation and Personal Tutor to win-condition access, and add a target that measures Approach in hand WITH seven mana available rather than Approach merely drawn.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 0.495 win-access figure measures drawing one of three cards and the record says the binding constraint is mana in the window. engine.json's proposed_goldfish_edits already flags the Mind Stone omission; no declared target measures the deck's actual win.

open_questions.question: How many land slots should a deck whose only win route costs seven mana twice run, and what do strong Approach of the Second Sun lists actually play as a land count and a tutor package?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 37-39 band is the generic control override from strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection and strategy.md has no section on alternate win conditions. The prescription raises lands 33 to 35 by construction-count reasoning, not from a measured figure for this shape of deck, and no deck_recon.json exists.

gaps: TWO VERDICTS HAVE NOW BEEN WITHDRAWN FROM THIS DOCUMENT, AND THE SECOND WITHDRAWAL IS THIS REVISION'S MAIN CONTENT. Round 1 said protection binds; that rested on a cast count, the pilot's want and one log game on a five-versions-old list. Round 2 replaced it with a causal mana claim resting on lands per GLOBAL turn (0.2279 against 0.1976, ci95 [-0.0489, -0.0117]) — and that denominator is the confound rather than a control for it, because global_turn keeps counting after this seat is eliminated and elimination differs 0.33 against 0.70 between the arms (the global-to-own-turn ratio is 4.10 in eliminated games against 3.68 in survived ones). On the seat's OWN turns the rate is 0.8178 against 0.7849, ci95 [-0.0960, +0.0301]; among the 46 games heliod survived, lands read 10.06 against 9.11, ci95 [-2.5120, +0.6152], and every other arm collapses too. That is the same test that correctly demoted the commander split in round 2, applied to round 2's own pair. The mana-base prescription stands on the audit's deterministic figures; the causal claim does not and is gone.

THE ROUND-2 COMMANDER CROSS-TABS WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE. They read 19/67 against 18/52 and 9/35 against 28/84, carrying 37 wins across 119 games when the seat won 20 of 99 decided. The cause was reading the winner from the LOG's 'has won' line, which names a last seat standing in the 20 clock-outs the record deliberately leaves without a winner. From records games[].winner: resolving 13/68 = 0.191 against 7/52 = 0.135, Newcombe diff -0.0566, ci95 [-0.1849, +0.0838]; flipping 6/35 = 0.171 against 14/85 = 0.165, diff -0.0067, ci95 [-0.1748, +0.1230]. Both span zero, so the conclusion holds, but the resolving split is directionally INVERTED from what was published — resolving the commander is associated with winning slightly more, not less — and engine.json (critic pass) already carried 6/35 against 14/85. Take the winner from the record, never from the log.

FORGE CANNOT MEASURE THE RESPONSE SIDE OF PROTECTION, which is why the axis reads adequate rather than vindicated or condemned. The threat side it measures well: 50 Heliod exits in 120 games, removed in 37 of the 68 games he resolved in, attributed 22 targeted / 16 opposing wraths / 5 own / 7 unattributed. The response side it does not measure at all: Guardian of Faith 0 casts (6 discards), Teferi's Protection 0 casts, Karametra's Blessing 9 casts of which 2 resolved on Heliod, Lightning Greaves 41 activations of which 5 attached to Heliod. Cast and activation counts in engine_casts.by_card are EVENTS, not games — three figures in the round-1 document mis-stated them as games — though 'cast in 29 games' for the Greaves is true as written, since those 29 casts fall in 29 distinct games.

THE EXIT TABLE CHANGED BETWEEN ROUND 2 AND ROUND 3 AND THIS IS THE SETTLED VERSION. Round 2 published 22 targeted / 12 opposing wraths / 2 own / 14 unattributed, from a window search spanning -14 to +9 lines around each Zone Change, which mis-attributes when two spells resolve close together. Attributing instead to the NEXT `Resolve Stack:` line — Forge logs the destroyed permanent's Zone Change immediately BEFORE the causing spell resolves — gives 22 / 16 / 5 / 7, i.e. 43 attributed, and it cross-checks against the record's zone split of 40 Graveyard and 10 Exile (the 10 exiles being Farewell 5, Swords to Plowshares 3, Chaos Mutation 2). MYSTIC GATE WAS DROPPED FOR A WRONG REASON IN ROUND 1 AND IS NOT RESTORED HERE. The stated ground — that mana-analysis would file it under sources.gated beside Skycloud Expanse — is false: manabase.gated_colour_source('Mystic Gate') returns False and land_colors reads it as {U, W}. The real reason to prefer Tundra and Sea of Clouds is that both make a coloured mana off the tap alone, while Mystic Gate's coloured mode needs a {W/U} from somewhere else first; whether a filter land is the right fifth source is a live question this document does not settle.

findings.note: THE NEW VERDICT'S LOAD-BEARING SENTENCE DOES NOT HOLD. 'It is the only gate that survives its confound' and axes[0]'s 'the figure that rules out game length as the explanation' both rest on lands per GLOBAL TURN (0.2279 vs 0.1976, Welch [-0.0489, -0.0117]). I reproduce that figure exactly -- and the denominator is the confound, not a control for it. global_turn keeps counting after heliod is eliminated, and elimination is precisely what differs between the arms: 9 of 27 Approach-cast games (0.33) against 65 of 93 no-Approach games (0.70); the global_turn-to-own-turn ratio is 4.10 in eliminated games against 3.68 in survived ones, so the arm with more eliminations is divided by a larger number for a mechanical reason. Two controls, both from the record's own fields: (a) on per_seat.turns -- the turns heliod actually took -- the rate is 0.8178 vs 0.7849, Welch +0.0329, ci95 [-0.0301, +0.0960], SPANS ZERO; (b) restricted to the 46 games heliod was not eliminated in, every arm of the comparison collapses -- lands 10.06 vs 9.11 ci95 [-0.615, +2.512], lands per global turn ci95 [-0.0044, +0.0435], lands per own turn ci95 [-0.0866, +0.0853], all spanning zero. The association is carried by the games heliod was eliminated in, which is the same 'these games are shorter' mechanism the doctor correctly used in gaps[1] to demote the commander split. THE PRESCRIPTION IS NOT REFUTED: 33 lands against a 37-39 band, 25 W and 26 U sources against 36, benchmark missed_land_drop_rate 0.2568 worst at turn six, and a finisher costing seven mana twice are deterministic and need no cross-tab. What must go is the claim that the Forge split establishes causation -- state it as an association and rest the axis on the audit.

The commander cross-tabs do not reproduce and one is directionally inverted. Claimed: resolving 19/67 = 0.284 against 18/52 = 0.346; flipping 9/35 against 28/84. Re-derived from record b0f44e4a games[].per_seat.heliod (winner == 'heliod' against commander_resolved_turn / commander_transformed_turn): resolving 13/68 = 0.191 against 7/52 = 0.135; flipping 6/35 = 0.171 against 14/85 = 0.165. The claimed figures carry 37 wins across 119 games when the seat won 20 of 99 decided, and the 84 in '28/84' should be 85. The resolving split is inverted: the record says resolving is associated with winning slightly MORE, not less. engine.json (critic verdict pass, today) already carries 6/35 against 14/85, so the diagnosis now contradicts a critic-passed artifact on the same table. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES with the right numbers and should be re-stated with them: Newcombe on resolving 13/68 vs 7/52 gives diff -0.0566, ci95 [-0.1849, +0.0838]; on flipping 6/35 vs 14/85, diff -0.0067, ci95 [-0.1748, +0.1230]. Both span zero.

The rewritten exit table is wrong on the two wrath columns, and my round-1 table is confirmed. Claimed: 22 targeted / 12 opposing wraths / 2 own / 14 unattributed. Re-derived by attributing each of the 50 exits to the next `Resolve Stack:` line (Forge logs the destroyed permanents' Zone Changes IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the causing spell's resolution) and identifying the caster from the matching `Add To Stack: Ai(N)-mm-<slug> cast <card>`: 22 targeted (Generous Gift 8, Stroke of Midnight 7, Swords to Plowshares 3, Aura Mutation 2, Chaos Mutation 2), 16 opposing wraths (Farewell 5, Wrath of God 4, Cleansing Nova 3, Hour of Reckoning 2, Austere Command 2), 5 own wraths, 7 unattributed. Caster is not in doubt: data/opponents/*/decklist.txt shows giada-angels runs Wrath of God, Farewell, Cleansing Nova, Austere Command, Generous Gift, Stroke of Midnight and Swords; baylen-tokens Aura Mutation and Hour of Reckoning; abaddon Blasphemous Act and Chaos Mutation. By zone the totals cross-check: 40 Graveyard + 10 Exile = 50, and the 7 unattributed are all Graveyard, so 33 destroy + 10 exile = 43 attributed.

'2 of Heliod's 50 battlefield exits (Day of Judgment 1, Supreme Verdict 1)' is 5 (Day of Judgment 2, Supreme Verdict 3). Only heliod runs either card in this pod, so attribution is certain the moment the spell is named. I printed all five with context: part-00 line 5016 (Day of Judgment, with giada's Flawless Maneuver resolving first to save their own board), part-01 line 21607 (Supreme Verdict), part-03 lines 13312 and 20680 (both Supreme Verdict, each with `Add To Stack: Ai(2)-mm-heliod cast Supreme Verdict` two lines above the exit block) and part-03 line 39042 (Day of Judgment). The doctor's gaps[0] honestly flags the disagreement with round 1 rather than burying it; this settles it at 5. THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED -- 5 of 50 exits against 56 own-wrath resolutions is still a small minority and still a piloting note. The same 2 propagates to cut_candidates[5].why and add_candidates[6].evidence.own_sweeper_exits_of_50.

'22 of 36 attributed' and evidence.targeted_exits_of_36_attributed. The attributed set is 43 (22 targeted + 16 opposing wraths + 5 own), not 36, so shroud/hexproof covers 22 of 43 (0.51), not 22 of 36 (0.61). The card argument is untouched and is the best-evidenced add in the document -- targeted removal is the single largest attributed cause of Heliod's exits either way, and log 001's redirected Swords is that event. Two qualifications the entry could carry: the Boots must be attached (Forge attached Greaves to Heliod 5 times in 120 games), and hexproof does not stop the 5 targeted EXILES (Swords 3, Chaos Mutation 2) from being cast at a legal target before it is equipped.

'Indestructible answers 30 of the 36 attributed exits' is 33 of 43 -- every Graveyard-zone exit is a 'destroy' effect and there are 33 of them (22 targeted less the 5 targeted exiles = 17, plus 11 opposing destroy-wraths, plus the 5 own). The entry's own evidence block is internally inconsistent with its prose: exile_exits_not_covered is 6, while the prose names 'the 5 targeted exiles or Farewell's exile-all', which is 5 + 5 = 10. The record's zone split settles it: 10 exits to Exile (Farewell 5, Swords to Plowshares 3, Chaos Mutation 2), 40 to Graveyard. So Mithril Coat's indestructible covers 33 of 43 attributed and misses 10.

'What gates that is MANA' -- where 'that' is reaching a SECOND Approach cast -- is contradicted by the doctor's own open_questions[0], which reports that lands do not separate the 12 two-cast games from the 15 one-cast games (9.58 against 9.67). I reproduce it: Welch ci95 [-2.054, +2.221] on lands and [-0.074, +0.154] on lands per own turn, both spanning zero, with global turn 41.17 against 43.20 and tutor casts 0.75 against 0.80. The mana evidence bears on casting Approach AT ALL (27 games of 120), not on converting one cast into two, and converting is the step that wins. open_questions[0] states this squarely and is the strongest question in the document; the verdict should inherit its caveat rather than assert the chain through a step the same artifact calls unexplained.

'12 of 12 with a second Approach cast won (Wilson [0.757, 1.000])' is exact -- I reproduce 12/12, 1/10, 7/77 over the 99 decided games and wilson_bounds(12,12) = [0.7575, 1.0] -- but it is close to definitional: Approach's oracle text wins the game on resolution when cast from hand with a prior cast, so the only way the ratio falls below 1.0 is a countered or fizzled second cast. Its actual informational content is that the pod never countered one: 39 casts and 39 resolutions across the 120 games, zero counters in the logs. Worth one clause, because as written a reader can take it for a discovered association rather than a card doing what it says against an AI that never answered it.

The entry's difficulty is 'easy' and its cost_of_cutting opens 'PAINFUL relative to its reputation'. One of the two is wrong on its face. On the evidence assembled I read 'easy' as right -- it is a like-for-like swap into Swiftfoot Boots, hexproof strictly dominates shroud for a deck that wants to target its own commander, and the AI used the Greaves as commander insurance 5 times in 120 games -- so the prose word is the one to drop. Flagging it because `difficulty` is the field a reader sorts on and the two fields must not disagree.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND IT IS THE STRONGEST THING IN THE REVISION. The heliod seat index does rotate: games 0-29 (part-00) Ai(1), 30-59 (part-01) Ai(4), 60-89 (part-02) Ai(3), 90-119 (part-03) Ai(2) -- exactly 30 games per position. A parser hardcoded to Ai(1) sees part-00 only, which holds 15 games with a commander resolve: the claimed '15 of 120' is exact. The corrected parse reproduces the record on every count I could test: 91 commander cast events (by_card cast 91), 44 flip activations (activated 44), 68 games with a resolve (games_resolved 68), 35 games with a transform (transformed.games 35) and 50 battlefield exits. I also verified record-to-log alignment before trusting any joined figure: 120 of 120 games match on `round`, and the only winner disagreements are the 20 truncated games, where the record deliberately records no winner and the log names a last seat standing -- the documented clock-out behaviour.

Every statistic in the new verdict reproduces from the record and logs, sign conventions aside: 12/12, 1/10, 7/77 over 99 decided games; Wilson [0.757, 1.000]; Approach-cast games 9.63 lands against 8.06 (Welch 1.5651, ci95 [0.4551, 2.6752]); 0.2279 lands per global turn against 0.1976 (Welch 0.0303, ci95 [0.0117, 0.0489]); 10 of the 12 second-Approach games never flipped him and 5 never cast him. My objection above is to the inference drawn from the last pair, not to the arithmetic.

The commander-split confound analysis is correct and honestly run, and it is the reason the round-1 verdict fell. Reproduced exactly: lands 9.04 against 7.60, global turn 43.06 against 38.98 (Welch -4.0781, ci95 [-6.8701, -1.286], excludes zero) and lands per global turn Welch 0.0134, ci95 [-0.0046, +0.0315], spanning zero. Applying that test to the doctor's own new pair is what produces my high finding; the test itself is the right one.
